note: Written by scripts/mutations.mjs. Every observed field here was produced by the run that performed the mutation; none of it is typed by hand. Re-run the script to reproduce it.

records.title: SIMON key words used left to right (printed order, not round-key order)
records.why: ePrint 2013/404 §3.2: "they are loaded into the shift registers with k0 on the right". Reading the printed words left to right gives a cipher that is self-consistent, decrypts its own ciphertext, and agrees with no published vector.

records.title: SPECK's 16-bit rotation amounts (7, 2) used at every word size
records.why: ePrint 2013/404 §4.1 fixes (alpha, beta) = (7, 2) only for n = 16 and (8, 3) otherwise. Hardcoding (7, 2) leaves SPECK32/64 passing, so a suite that tests only the smallest size cannot see it.

records.title: SIMON's constant sequence read from the wrong end
records.why: ePrint 2013/404 §3.2 indexes round key i+m with (z_j)_i, reading the printed sequence left to right. Reading it right to left is a different cipher with the same structure.

records.title: GIFT-64 round key added at bit positions 4i+1 and 4i+2 (the GIFT-128 positions)
records.why: ePrint 2017/622 §2 puts GIFT-64’s round key at 4i and 4i+1, and GIFT-128’s at 4i+1 and 4i+2. The all-zero vector CANNOT see this: an all-zero round key XORs to nothing wherever it is placed. Vectors 2 and 3 can.

records.title: GIFT's key state rotation skipped
records.why: ePrint 2017/622 §2 updates the key state as k1 >>> 2 || k0 >>> 12 || k7 ... k2. Skipping the two rotations is invisible to the all-zero vector, whose key state is all zero however it is rotated.

records.title: SKINNY's state loaded column-wise instead of row-wise
records.why: ePrint 2016/660 §2: "the state is loaded row-wise rather than in the column-wise fashion we have come to expect from the AES". The transposed load costs nothing in self-consistency and every published vector.
records.replacement:
// MUTATION (6): column-wise load.

records.title: SKINNY's tweakey updated BEFORE it is XORed in
records.why: ePrint 2016/660 §2 applies AddRoundTweakey and then updates the arrays. Updating first shifts every round key by one round.
records.anchor:
addRoundTweakey(st, tk); // XOR in FIRST ...
    updateTweakey(tk, p.s); // ... then update
records.replacement:
updateTweakey(tk, p.s); // MUTATION (7): update BEFORE the XOR
    addRoundTweakey(st, tk);

records.title: PRINCE's SR applied as a scatter instead of a gather
records.why: ePrint 2012/529 §3.3 prints SR as a mapping whose direction the prose leaves implicit. Read as a scatter it is the inverse permutation, which is a different cipher.
records.anchor:

records.title: PRINCE's reflection decryption without adding alpha to the core key
records.why: ePrint 2012/529 §2: D_(k0||k0′||k1) = E_(k0′||k0||k1 XOR alpha). Swapping the whitening keys without adding alpha is the shape of the property with the constant that makes it true removed.

records.title: Rotational survival counted on one output word instead of both
records.why: A pair survives only if BOTH output words are rotationally related. At ONE round the two checks are provably equivalent (the second word is the first XOR a rotation-invariant term), which is why a single-round test cannot see this; from three rounds on they come apart by about 15%.

records.title: A cipher reported as "vectors pass" from a stored value instead of a live comparison
records.why: Invariant 1 says a cipher is offered only if every published vector reproduces, and it is enforced by RUNNING them at load. Replacing the comparison with the expected value makes the check vacuous — and invisible, because every cipher that ships here is correct. Only a deliberately broken module can tell the difference, which is what the owning test injects.

records.title: SPECK key words reversed (round-key order, not printed order)
records.why: The mirror of mutation (1). SPECK’s schedule takes the key in the order the paper PRINTS it — (l[m-2], ..., l[0], k[0]) — where SIMON’s wants it reversed. Applying SIMON’s convention to SPECK is the same class of error in the other direction.

records.title: The negative claim’s second clause deleted (§4.1d bite 1)
records.why: §4.1d requires the negative-claim test to bite: delete the text naming the limitation and assertion 3 must fail. What is left still says the round function has the property, which is the half that flatters the page.
records.replacement:
export const NEGATIVE_CLAIM =
  'Rotational pairs pass through SPECK’s round function with high probability.';

records.title: The real-schedule column fed rotated round keys by mistake (§4.1d bite 2)
records.why: §4.1d requires that breaking a check inside the fixture fails assertion 2. Feeding the real-schedule column rotated round keys makes survivors appear past two rounds, so the verdict loses its second clause and the negative claim stops rendering — the page would then be claiming the limitation without the evidence for it.

records.title: The control-boundary token degraded below WCAG 1.4.11’s 3:1
records.why: A gate is only worth what a mutation proves. This restores --border-strong to #3a554d, the value this lab actually shipped until the gate measured it at 2.14:1 against --panel, and requires the a11y run to fail NAMING the non-text contrast finding. Without this, the contrast oracle could be dead and every run would still be green.

records.title: The global border-box removed, reintroducing the 380px reflow failure
records.why: The other half of the same argument: the reflow oracle is the only check for WCAG 1.4.10, because axe has no rule for it at all. Removing border-box returns .cl-hero-why to a 384px box inside a 348px container, and the phone-width run must fail naming the horizontal scroll.
